newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KBB SEES LOWER FULL-YEAR ORDINARY NET.
newsitem.headline: KBB SEES LOWER FULL-YEAR ORDINARY NET.

text.p: Dutch store chain Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer said on Wednesday it expected full-year net from ordinary operations in the 1996/97 financial year ending January 31 to lag significantly behind that of the previous year.
"The net result from ordinary operations of KBB is expected to lag significantly behind that of last year," the department store chain said in a statement.
It said it had updated its in-house results prognosis for the 1996/97 financial year on the basis of its provisional result to September.
The update was prompted by the decision of Dutch retail and business services group Vendex to divest its 36 percent KBB stake, the company said.
Developments to date had confirmed the positive trends of the first half in specialty and department stores, it said.
But an exception was its clothing chain M&S Mode, where the negative trend of the first half-year had continued into the first months of the second half-year, KBB said.
It added that the final months of the year were of crucial importance to its full-year result.

"However, presuming that the positive retail trading climate will not deteriorate but that the disappointing trend at M&S Mode will continue, the net result from ordinary operations of KBB is expected to lag significantly behind that of last year," the store chain said.

Vendex said on Tuesday it planned to sell its KBB stake, acquired in the 1970s, because there were few short-term prospects of closer cooperation between the two. Consequently Vendex no longer regarded KBB as a strategic holding, it said.
The shares are to be sold in a placement expected to be completed within two weeks. The sell-off could generate up to 620 million guilders, market watchers say.
KBB shares ended Wednesday's session on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange up 1.90 guilders at 142.00, after losing 6.10 guilders to 140.10 on Tuesday's divestment news.
In March, KBB reported 1995/96 net from ordinary operations fell 20 percent to 98.6 million guilders from a year-earlier 122.7 million guilders.
